images.title: Drag one value, watch the mean
images.purpose: Recap the drag the outlier activity: moving one value far out shifts the mean a lot but leaves the median where it was.
images.composition: Two short dot plots, Before above After, on the same scale, with one curved arrow showing the dragged dot; white space on the right.
exact_structure: Two dark grey (#2B2B2B) number lines from 0 to 30, one above the other, each with small ticks every 2 and numbered ticks at 0, 10, 20 and 30.

Top line, labelled Before: 5 teal (#0072B2) dots at 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8; at 6 the reddish purple (#CC79A7) median triangle sits just under the line, labelled Median = 6, with the amber (#E69F00) mean triangle directly under it, labelled Mean = 6.

Bottom line, labelled After: 5 dots, 4 teal dots at 4, 5, 6 and 7 and 1 vermilion (#D55E00) dot at 28; reddish purple median triangle at 6 labelled Median = 6; amber mean triangle at 10 labelled Mean = 10.
A grey (#6B7280) curved arrow runs from the dot at 8 on the top line to the vermilion dot at 28 on the bottom line.
The median triangles are vertically aligned at 6 in both rows; the mean triangle moves from 6 to 10.
rejection: a number of dots other than 5 on either line
the median triangle moved in the After row
the mean triangle in the After row at a value other than 10
the two lines on different scales
images.takeaway: Dragging one value far away moves the mean towards it, but the median stays put.
images.description: Two dot plots: before, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 with mean and median 6; after the 8 is dragged to 28, the mean is 10 and the median is still 6.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to predict where the mean triangle will land before showing the After row, then try it in the activity.

image_decisions.why: A before and after picture fixes the idea the drag activity explores, so the doer has a reference.
